Hi Alex - thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of the call and a few clarifying questions so we can size pricing:

Recap:
- Use case: clinical note summarization + search augmentation (hybrid embedding + generation) for internal clinician UX.
- Target latency: sub-second for median; < 500ms for interactive flows.
- Data sensitivity: PHI; interested in Private deployment options if pilot looks good.

Clarifying questions (to confirm numbers for unit economics):
1) Estimated monthly token volume (best guess): average + peak?
2) Average tokens per request and 95/99th percentile tokens (helps with batching assumptions).
3) Peak concurrent requests / QPS during highest traffic windows.
4) Target budget range (monthly) or target $/1M tokens you're aiming for so we can recommend commitment vs hosted vs dedicated.

Notes on batching/concurrency: our cost model assumes continuous batching across short windows (10-50ms) to aggregate requests. The effective per-token unit cost improves as requests are collinear (similar sequence lengths) and as concurrency increases; if you have steady traffic of 10-20 concurrent requests we typically see meaningful batching benefits.

I've attached a high-level pricing sheet and a short example unit-econ calc. Once you share the numbers above I can send a tailored ROI calc and propose an SOW/pilot.

Next steps:
- Alex: send token volumes + avg tokens per request + peak concurrency
- We'll produce an expected $/1M tokens band (hosted vs dedicated) and a proposed 30-day pilot.

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Follow-up: Cost/Batching discussion - Acme Health (internal note)

Camila - quick internal note before you respond to Alex. Based on Alex's numbers here are some suggested lifts and a draft calc we can include:

Assumptions & suggested pricing:
- Traffic: 120M tokens / month; avg 350 tokens/req => ~342k requests/day (~4 req/s average), with 8-12 concurrent typical and 30 concurrency spike.
- Recommend running hosted pilot for 30 days with a benchmark, then move to Dedicated if steady (annual reserved commit) to reach target unit economics.

Example unit economics (ballpark for discussion):
- Hosted baseline: $250 / 1M tokens (no commit), so 120M => $30k / month.
- Dedicated (reserved) with moderate commit: $140-180 / 1M tokens depending on padding and sustained concurrency; at $150 / 1M => $18k / month.
- Dedicated + continuous batching improvements and prefix caching (expected given many similar prompts): additional 15-25% effective savings on token compute => effective $/1M could approach $110-130 in steady state.

Batching & concurrency guidance to include in email to Alex:
- Continuous batching benefits depend on request arrival patterns. With median inter-arrival times that allow micro-batches (10-50ms) and 8-12 concurrent requests we should see meaningful batching; spikes to 30 concurrency are fine but we should size pools to handle the spike without falling back to slower fallback models.
- For interactive targets (P95 < 500ms) we recommend a small reserved buffer of capacity (burst capacity or higher-priority lanes) to keep tail latency low during spikes.

Proposed pilot: 30-day hosted trial with a benchmark plan: run representative traffic (we'll replay a 48-72 hour window from your export), collect latency/throughput, and produce final unit-econ calc + SOW. Offer: $0.00 for first 50M tokens of the pilot (credit) or 20% off hosted list for first 30 days if procurement needs a contract.

I'll draft the ROI table and attach SOW-draft.docx. LMK when you want me to send.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Alex - thanks for the quick numbers, very helpful. Summary + proposal below (copying Marissa who will run the bench):

Summary of what you sent:
- 120M tokens/month estimate; avg 350 tokens/req; P95 ~950 tokens; spikes to 30 concurrency briefly.
- Target budget <= $150 / 1M tokens.

Preliminary proposal:
- Pilot: 30-day hosted pilot with a replay of 48-72 hours from your export. Options: first 50M tokens free credit OR 20% off hosted list for the month.
- Expected unit economics (pre-benchmark): hosted list ~$250 / 1M => ~ $30k/mo. With a committed dedicated pool we can push to ~$140-180 / 1M ($16.8k- $21.6k/mo). With batching/prefix caching we often see extra 15-25% savings - realistic target for you: $110-150 / 1M tokens depending on commit and caching.
- Latency: with continuous batching and a small reserved buffer we expect median sub-second and P95 typically < 500ms for interactive flows; we'll size burst capacity to keep the tail tight during the 10-15 minute spikes.

Next steps / ask list:
1) Alex: confirm pilot option (50M credit vs 20% off) and sign the attached SOW-draft.docx if procurement prefers a contract to start.
2) Alex: confirm a 48-72 hour representative window from acme_usage_export.csv for benchmark.
3) We will schedule a 30-45 minute kickoff with Marissa and infra to agree success criteria (latency targets, throughput, and evaluation metrics).

If you want an immediate ballpark number to share with finance: at $140 / 1M tokens your monthly inference spend at 120M tokens would be ~$16,800. If you want us to aim closer to $110 / 1M we can show the path (dedicated + prefix caching + 12-16 concurrent steady traffic).

Would you be open to a quick call Thursday to finalize the pilot?
